name: NQO1
notes: EC 1.6.5.2 is given by the paper (Introduction) and is also the EC in UniProt P15559. Recombinant human NQO1 expressed from pET-46 Ek/LIC in E. coli BL21(DE3) and purified by IMAC, i.e. an N-terminally His-tagged full-length construct; 0.97-0.99 mol FAD per monomer. Residue numbering matches the P15559 sequence at every residue the paper names: Y127, Y129, R139, Y156, H162, P187, S82 (Fig. 1 legend states that numbering follows the full-length sequence). pdb left empty: RCSB lists 29 entries for P15559 (searched 2026-11-09, UniProt-accession search) - too many to vet as exactly WT - and the paper names no PDB entry; no RCSB entry cites the paper's DOI 10.3390/antiox9090772.

name: CvPheH
notes: Paper gives no EC number; 1.14.16.1 is the EC of UniProt P30967. The paper names no strain; the plasmid came from P. Frey and the gene was subcloned into pET21b and expressed in E. coli BL21(DE3), full length, no tag described. Numbering matches P30967: position 234 is Ile, consistent with the I234D mutation. PDB entries found by searching RCSB for P30967 (14 entries) and by sequence; the 7 listed carry no engineered mutation. Sequence differences RCSB lists that this study did not engineer: 1LTU, 1LTV, 1LTZ, 3TCY and 4JPY differ from P30967 at M64L, Q85E, V276I and R288H (isolate differences); 3TCY, 3TK2 and 3TK4 are 302-residue constructs with an N-terminal GPLGS/GLPGS tag remnant, and 3TK2/3TK4 otherwise match P30967 exactly. Entries with other engineered mutations were excluded: 4ESM (Y155A), 4ETL (F258A), 4JPX (S203P), 4Q3W-4Q3Z (D139E/N/A/K). No RCSB entry cites this paper's DOI 10.1021/bi801295w.

name: CvPheH
notes: Single mutant made by QuikChange in pET21b-CvPheH; the paper introduced it as the counterpart of the rat PheH V379D mutation, to unmask the intrinsic isotope effect. Position 234 of P30967 is Ile, so the paper's numbering matches UniProt. pdb empty: of the 14 RCSB entries for P30967 none carries a substitution at residue 234 (checked by comparing each entity sequence with P30967; the pdbx_mutation field is empty for all 14, including entries whose titles name mutations). No RCSB entry cites 10.1021/bi801295w.

name: PtmT2
notes: The accession A0A023VSF1 is given by the paper itself (Experimental Section: 'The PtmT2 gene from S. platensis (UniProtKB accession code A0A023VSF1, amino acid sequence 1-533)'). That UniProt entry is unreviewed and carries no EC number, and the paper gives none, so ec is empty. Construct: residues 1-533 with an N-terminal His6 tag in pet22b+, expressed in E. coli BL21 (DE3) - full length, not truncated. The catalytic acid D313 of the conserved DDXD motif matches position 313 (Asp) of A0A023VSF1, so the paper's numbering matches UniProt. PDB 5BP8 is named by the paper (used for the modelling) and is the only RCSB entry for A0A023VSF1; its deposited sequence is 523 residues beginning at A0A023VSF1 residue 6 and carrying SNA in place of AQP at positions 6-8 (a cloning remnant that this study did not engineer), otherwise identical. 5BP8's primary citation is 10.1021/jacs.6b04317 (the paper's ref 13); no RCSB entry cites this paper's DOI 10.1002/cbic.201700443.

name: Kemp eliminase KE07
organism: none - computationally designed enzyme; scaffold imidazole glycerol phosphate synthase (HisF) from Thermotoga maritima; expressed in Escherichia coli BL21(DE3)
notes: Computationally designed enzyme with no natural counterpart: the Kemp elimination has no natural enzyme and no EC number, and the paper and UniProt assign none, so ec is empty (the scaffold's own EC 4.3.2.10 belongs to a different reaction). The uniprot field holds the SCAFFOLD accession: the paper says the theozyme 'was then grafted into the scaffold of imidazole glycerol phosphate synthase (HisF) from Thermotoga maritima' = UniProt Q9X0C6. The paper's residue numbering matches Q9X0C6 exactly at every position it names (I7, V12, W50, F77, E101, I102, Y128, K146, G202, K222, N224, F229); PDB entries of this series number one higher because the deposited construct has an extra Ala after the initiator Met. Relative to Q9X0C6 the KE07 design carries M1A (insertion), C9A, D11I, T21S, V48S, L50W, S101E, A128Y, D130A, L169V, T171G, D176L, S201H, L222K, A224N and F227L, plus a C-terminal GSLEHHHHHH extension (the paper: C-terminal His6 tags, pET-29b(+) in E. coli BL21(DE3)). Mutation sets below are given in the paper's (= Q9X0C6) numbering, read from the RCSB entity sequences. The main text names only some of them (R1->R4: I7D, K146E, G202R, N224D; R5: V12M; R6: K146T; R7/R7-2: F77I, F229S, I102F); the full lists are in Supplementary Table 1, which was not available. L227F, present in every evolved variant, is a reversion to the HisF residue and is not named in the main text. No substitution relative to the KE07 design. None of these four entries cites this paper's DOI (they carry no primary citation in RCSB); the ten entries that do cite 10.1038/s41467-018-06305-y are 6C7H, 6C7M, 6C7T, 6C7V, 6C8B, 6CAI, 6CT3, 6DC1, 6DKV and 6DNJ. 6C7H is the same design carrying W50A (Trp50Ala) and is therefore not listed here; no isotope effect was entered for a Trp50Ala variant.

name: TaCPa2E
notes: The paper gives no EC number and there is no UniProt entry for this protein, so ec is empty; the glossary expands TaCPa2E as 'Thermodesulfatator atlanticus CDP-paratose 2-epimerase', and UniProt gives EC 5.1.3.10 for the homologous Salmonella CDP-paratose/CDP-tyvelose 2-epimerase P14169. uniprot empty: rest.uniprot.org (searched 2026-11-09) holds only two T. atlanticus proteins (C0MPG6 and C0MPG7, dissimilatory sulfite reductase subunits) and the paper names no accession (it refers to ref 72, Appl. Environ. Microbiol. 2021, 10.1128/AEM.02131-20). RCSB cross-references PDB 9RL0 to UniProt A0ABS1GJY6, but UniProt assigns that accession to Persephonella atlantica and its sequence differs from the 9RL0 sequence at 49 of 340 positions (about 86 % identity), so it is not the wild-type accession of this enzyme. PDB 9RL0 ('CDP-tyvelose 2-epimerase from Thermodesulfatator atlanticus', released 2026-06-10) is this wild-type enzyme: its 340-residue deposited sequence has Tyr164 - the catalytic base the paper names - and an average mass of 39362.4 Da, matching the paper's stated TaCPa2E_WT monomer mass of 39362 g/mol, and its depositors include Rapp C. and Nidetzky B. Its primary citation is 10.1016/j.jbc.2026.111384; no RCSB entry cites this paper's DOI 10.1021/acscatal.2c00257, and the paper itself names no PDB entry. Construct: C-terminal His tag, pET21a in E. coli BL21 (DE3); homodimer, each subunit with tightly bound NAD+; the paper gives no strain. The Y164F variant was also made but was inactive (>=10^4-fold lower specific rate) and yielded no isotope effect, so it has no row.
